item.title: After injury setbacks, Sami Terra leads Shaker boys' soccer into state regionals
item.description: Shaker senior Sami Terra gets a foot on the ball in front of Guilderland senior Jack Wasserbach during the Section 2, Class AAA finals on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at LaSalle Institute in Troy, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) Sami Terra began his Shaker boys' varsity soccer career with a hat trick. Last Saturday, the senior had another, this time helping the Blue Bison win a sectional championship . Between those performances came injury setbacks, a brief return to the field and months spent trying to get healthy enough to play again. Terra scored all three goals in Shaker's 3-1 win over Guilderland in the Section 2 Class AAA final, sending the No. 6-ranked Blue Bison into Saturday's 4:30 p.m. state regional at Waterford-Halfmoon against Section 3's Cicero-North Syracuse (16-3), which is ranked 12th in the state. With 17 goals this season, up from eight last year, Terra has returned to top form just in time to help lead Shaker (13-5) into its biggest games of the season. "Sami's been a goal scorer his whole life," Shaker coach Dan Fountain said. "He's had high expectations on him from Day 1. … He's an unbelievably amazing striker." Terra put his talents on display in his varsity debut last season, scoring three goals in a 5-0 win over Albany. But a hip injury interrupted his junior season, leaving him on the sideline before he returned in time for the postseason, which ended on penalty kicks against Guilderland. Another hip injury while playing for his club team extended his struggles into the offseason and he wasn't cleared to return until just before Shaker's tryouts this year. Terra, who plays club soccer for New York Elite Alleycats FC after growing up in Shaker's Saints FC program, said the long absence gave him time to think about what he wanted from his final high school season. "I missed soccer for so long, and I didn't have the chance to play with my team and stuff," Terra said. "Making this comeback, it just means a lot." He missed the first few games and eased back in slowly. "I think he's gotten better and better as the season's gone on, as he's gotten healthier and gotten used to playing again," Fountain said. "He just created so much for us offensively." Terra scored the deciding goals in 2-1 wins over Niskayuna and Averill Park, all four goals in a 4-1 victory over CBA and twice in a 3-0 win over Colonie this season. He added a goal in Shaker's 2-0 sectional semifinal win over Saratoga Springs before his hat trick against Guilderland. In the final, he scored on a free kick with 4.3 seconds left before halftime, headed in Liam Gregory's free kick to break a 1-1 tie and completed his hat trick on a breakaway. Even when Terra wasn't scoring, he drew defenders and created opportunities for teammates. "Sami's very smart, so he runs off the ball well," Fountain said. item.title: Reason given for why Dowman’s appeal was rejected
item.description: Reason given for why Dowman’s appeal was rejected Max Dowman will have to serve the remaining two domestic matches of his suspension after Arsenal failed in their appeal against his red card during the match against Fleetwood Town. The Gunners had hoped to have the teenager’s punishment overturned or reduced, but the decision has now been upheld. The 16-year-old was sent off after reacting to a rough challenge from an opponent. Dowman was unhappy with the tackle and responded in a way that left the referee with little choice but to take disciplinary action. His reaction also reportedly disappointed Mikel Arteta , who had warned his players to expect physical challenges during the game. Although Dowman will have to learn from the incident, the experience could help him develop greater composure as he continues his progress at senior level. Arsenal lose appeal against suspension Arsenal challenged the original decision in the hope of making Dowman available sooner, but their appeal was rejected. An independent panel has now explained why it believed the suspension should remain unchanged. According to Standard Sport , members of the panel highlighted that Dowman had an opportunity to avoid escalating the incident after being tackled. They felt his response justified the referee’s decision to send him off. The panel stated that he had the chance “to step out of this challenge without any reaction, but he turned back towards Neal and his forceful attempt at a retaliatory kick gave the referee a decision to make”. (Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images) Dowman must wait for another opportunity The suspension comes at an inconvenient time for Arsenal, with Bukayo Saka currently injured and an opportunity potentially opening up for Dowman to feature more regularly. The youngster will now miss two further domestic fixtures, preventing him from taking advantage of the immediate opening in the squad. However, his suspension should be completed before Saka is expected to return, meaning he could still have opportunities to make an impression. Dowman will hope to receive more minutes once he is available again, particularly if Arsenal encounter further injury problems in their attacking positions. item.description: Red Sox Floated as Landing Spot for Former Braves All-Star on $54M Deal originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Many of the top names available on the free agency market regarding starting pitchers have been floated as options for the Boston Red Sox this winter. However, some other guys haven't been mentioned who might make just as much sense. The interesting question for the Red Sox is whether they want to spend on another high-end starter or go with a more under-the-radar option who can get outs at a high level. Among those who fit the latter, Arizona Diamondbacks free agent Michael Soroka might be an even better option than some are considering. Soroka, not too old at 29 years old, is coming off his best season yet, posting a 3.41 ERA in 22 appearances and 21 starts. He struck out 114 hitters in 116 innings. With the expectation that the Red Sox are going to add a starter, The Athletic recently named Boston as a potential fit for the right-hander, predicting that he'd land a three-year, $54 million contract. “A 21-year-old All-Star in 2019, Soroka had his meteoric rise derailed for three-plus seasons because of Achilles, hamstring and shoulder injuries. He bounced from the Braves to the White Sox to the Nationals and, in 2026, to the Diamondbacks, where he had his best season since that standout rookie campaign, throwing 116 innings and making 21 starts. “He had two more IL stints, but his success when healthy provided more reason to believe — or, at least, hope — that he can still be the impact starter of his youth. His chase rate, hard-hit rate and walk rate were all in the 80th percentile or better. Durability concerns will, of course, hamper his market, but the upside is sufficient to maintain significant interest,” The Athletic’s Tim Britton wrote . The question with Soroka has obviously been those injuries throughout his career, as there were points with the Atlanta Braves when there was an argument to be made that he was among the best young starters in baseball earlier in his career. Those injuries slowed him down a bit, as he struggled a ton with the Chicago White Sox and Washington Nationals in 2024 and 2025 in comparison to what he did in Atlanta prior to that. I wouldn't say that he got back to what he was back in the day in 2026, but he looked a lot better, and that's something that's likely going to interest teams like the Red Sox. ICC sets sights on China to target its next 500 million cricket fans The International Cricket Council (ICC) has revealed an ambitious 10-year strategic roadmap focused on transforming China into a competitive force in international cricket. Speaking in an interview with the Global Times , ICC Chief Executive Officer Sanjog Gupta highlighted China's regional stature and immense sporting footprint as pivotal drivers for the game's long-term global expansion. With cricket officially returning to the Olympic programme at the 2028 Los Angeles Games, the global governing body sees China as fertile ground for sustainable growth. Rather than viewing the country simply as a broadcast consumer base, the ICC is prioritising a grass-roots-to-high-performance ecosystem designed to cultivate elite homegrown talent. item.title: Golfers Gain Distance By Fixing Attack Angle Numbers
item.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Most avid golfers track their swing speed, yet many ignore the single metric that changes distance the most. Attack angle determines whether the club moves up or down at the moment of impact. This number dictates launch height and spin rates more than almost any other factor in the game. According to MyGolfSpy , a positive angle means the club moves upward, while a negative angle indicates a downward strike. The ideal number differs completely between the driver and irons, a fact that often confuses players who try to hit every club the same way. Understanding this distinction allows a golfer to maximize carry distance without increasing swing speed. MyGolfSpy reports that inconsistent attack angles can cause high-handicap players to see over 30 yards of carry variation. The same golfer with the same speed can hit shots 12 yards apart just by changing the angle of attack. This gap exists because the club path interacts with the ball differently depending on whether it is teed up or sitting on the turf. The Driver Requires an Upward Strike With the driver, the goal is to hit the ball on an upward strike. Golfers should tee the ball high and position it toward the front of the stance to facilitate this motion. MyGolfSpy explains that hitting up helps in two specific ways: it launches the ball higher and reduces spin. High launch combined with low spin creates the optimal conditions for maximum distance. Data provided by GOLFJOY and cited by MyGolfSpy shows a clear difference when comparing a -5 degree angle to a +5 degree angle. When a golfer swings at 80 mph, hitting down on the ball produces a lower trajectory with excessive spin that kills distance. Conversely, hitting up with a +5 degree angle optimizes the launch conditions. Reports note that the same swing speed yields vastly different results based solely on this vertical club path. Players who try to hit down on the driver are fighting the physics of the club design. Irons Demand a Slight Downward Angle Irons work in the opposite direction compared to the driver. The ball sits on the ground, so the club must strike the ball first and then the turf. This sequence ensures clean contact and proper spin to hold the green. MyGolfSpy states that the sweet spot for a 7-iron is roughly 2 to 5 degrees downward. Striking the ball with too little or too much downward angle costs significant distance. An 80 mph swing with a -4 degree angle produces a launch of 18 degrees, which represents the middle option that wins for most players. Deviating from this range leads to poor contact. If the angle is too flat, the club may catch the turf before the ball. If the angle is too steep, the player might thin the shot or lose energy transfer. The data shows that the middle option within the 2 to 5 degree range consistently delivers the best results for carry and control. item.title: Mets’ Johnny Washington Hire Leaves Braves Fans With Big Questions
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The New York Mets just made a move that stings for Atlanta fans. They hired Johnny Washington as a co-hitting coach, pulling him right from the Braves’ organization. Washington served as the Braves’ minor league hitting coordinator during the 2026 season. The Mets are now stacking three hitting coaches in one room, a setup that feels strange for a team that needs immediate offense. A Familiar Name in a New Spot Washington is not a stranger to the Mets. Andy Green, the current Mets manager, previously employed him with the San Diego Padres and subsequently the Chicago Cubs. The hiring was reported by Joel Sherman of the New York Post, who noted the Mets finally have a new coach after weeks of searching. They fired their previous hitting coordinator, Jeff Albert, after just one season in the role. Washington joins Troy Snitker and Rafael Fernandez. The situation looks odd because the Mets missed out on top targets. Prior to selecting Washington, they consulted John Mallee of the Chicago Cubs and Kevin Long of the Philadelphia Phillies. Each was considered a top contender to direct the staff. Instead, the Mets turned to a familiar voice from Green’s past. This choice suggests they could not land the big names they wanted. The Braves, meanwhile, kept Tim Hyers as their hitting coach despite a lackluster offensive season. Why the Braves Let Him Go Braves fans have to ask why Washington slipped through their fingers. The team kept Hyers even though the offense ranked eighth in runs but had the third-fewest walks in MLB. Their on-base percentage of .309 was a full point lower than the Mets. In 2026, only the Colorado Rockies and San Francisco Giants posted a lower on-base rate than Atlanta. Washington would have signaled a change, but the Braves chose stability over a new voice. item.title: Jessica Pegula jokes about 'hot mic' incident at WTA Finals media day
item.description: American tennis star Jessica Pegula wasted little time defusing the tension around the well-documented "hot mic" incident during her appearance with media Friday ahead of the WTA Finals. As Pegula entered the room and sat down at the front of the press conference, she grabbed the microphone and playfully tapped it and said "OK, the mic's on. Just wanted to be sure." Her joke drew a laugh from the assembled media. Pegula was referencing an incident that happened earlier in the week when a microphone on the practice court that was intended to just pick up ambient noise of tennis balls hitting the hardcourt and environmental sounds for a livestream, actually picked up a conversation between Pegula and one of her coaches during a practice session. On the live stream she was heard calling another tour player Mirra Andreeva a "diva" among other comments in what she thought was a private discussion. A spokesperson for Pegula has since reported that Pegula "had absolutely no idea that her conversation with (her coach) was being livestreamed and certainly never expected a private discussion during practice to be made public." Pegula has since apologized to the other players involved. For its part, the WTA has taken full responsibility and apologized to Pegula for the incident. On Friday, WTA Chair Valerie Camillo, who spoke to the media minutes before Pegula did, struck a different tone that Pegula's light-hearted opener. She was quite serious. She said livestreaming practices is an attempt to bring fans closer to the game and they have done it before, using the similar ambient noise effect, but in this case mistakes were made. "There were several breakdowns in our execution of the livestream, given our own policies and procedures. There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area and it was also not our intention to capture conversations on the livestream of practices but rather to record ambient sound. So clearly there was a failure in our technical execution. As the chair of the WTA I'm committed to leading an organization that delivers the best for our players, our tournaments and our fans. Our execution here did not meet that standard," she said. "I want to specifically apologize to Jessica Pegula, what happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest start and she does not deserve this distraction. One of the primary responsibilities of the WTA is to protect our players whenever possible. ANd that did not happen here. Players deserve better and we will continue to work to raise the bar at the WTA." Camillo went on to say that the sound has been disabled now on the practice courts for the rest of this event. item.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea injury scare ahead of Sunderland clash
item.description: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea injury scare ahead of Sunderland clash Chelsea Team News: Caicedo and Martinez Face Late Fitness Test for Sunderland Trip Chelsea head to Sunderland on Sunday with Xabi Alonso still waiting on two important calls, Moises Caicedo and Emi Martinez. The manager has made it clear that Saturday’s final training session will decide both cases, which tells you everything. No grand declarations, no guessing, just a straight medical and tactical call before facing the league’s bottom side. The bigger selection issue may well be in goal. Martinez has returned to training sooner than expected after jaw surgery and has been working in a protective mask. That gives Alonso a decision to make. Mike Penders, still only 21, has filled in during Martinez’s absence and, apart from one significant mistake, has done well enough. That matters. You do not rush a goalkeeper back unless he is genuinely ready, especially when the deputy has not looked out of his depth. Alonso said: “Tomorrow we have the last training session before Sunday and we will decide [then].” He added: “But he [Martinez] is training well. All the decisions are tough in all the positions, but it is very good that Emi has made a great effort to be back and is ahead of [the schedule]. Tomorrow we will check and Sunday we will take the final decision.” Caicedo Fitness Update Caicedo’s situation is slightly different. He started against Manchester United last weekend, but his training week has been interrupted by discomfort afterwards. Alonso was careful with his wording, which usually means a player is not fully clear yet. He said: “Well, after the last game he had little problems. We expect to check tomorrow. We have some different situations, and Moi is one of them. It is discomfort more than the [old] calf [injury].” That sounds manageable, but Chelsea will still want certainty before naming him in midfield. With the international break looming, there is little sense in forcing the issue. Photo IMAGO Hato Still Missing for Chelsea There is no such uncertainty over Jorrel Hato. He missed the United game and will miss this one too. Alonso’s update was blunt and definitive: “No, no, no, he is not fit. It will take him some more weeks to be fit.” Palmer Focus Remains on Chelsea Alonso was also asked about Cole Palmer after his recent England squad omission, despite Chelsea viewing him as fit. The manager refused to turn it into a saga. “No, we have not spoken about that,” Alonso said. “We are very happy with Cole. He is connecting very well with the other attackers and is helping the team.” That is the line Chelsea will stick to. Keep Palmer focused, assess Caicedo and Martinez on Saturday, and avoid making Sunday more complicated than it needs to be.

item.description: The big Iowa-Northwestern matchup got a Friday surprise, one day before the Nov. 7 kickoff at Ryan Field (6:30 p.m., FOX). ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported that star Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles, who had been listed as questionable on the first two injury reports of the week, will miss the game against the Hawkeyes with an upper-body injury. Nicco Marchiol, a left-handed transfer from West Virginia who has attempted one pass this season, is expected to make the start against an Iowa defense that ranks No. 4 nationally. Veteran back-up Nicco Marchiol will make the start for Northwestern, his first start for the Wildcats. He’s a veteran who has a 6-2 record as a starter while at West Virginia. He’s played in 27 career games. — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) November 6, 2026 The sudden move shifted the betting line. Iowa went from a 2½-point underdog to a 2½-point favorite as of early Friday afternoon. The 19th-ranked Hawkeyes (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten Conference) spoke earlier this week about wanting to atone for a poor 2024 performance against Chiles when he was with Michigan State and dominated Iowa, 32-20, in East Lansing. Chiles had been playing fantastic football, having thrown 13 touchdowns and rushed for 10 more with just one interception through eight games this fall. He has been the catalyst for Chip Kelly’s unique offense that catered to his dual-threat capabilities. And while it is seemingly a benefit for Iowa to face Northwestern (6-2, 3-2) without its star quarterback, it does throw a lot of preparations made all week into the trash can. While Northwestern probably won’t change its style of offense, Marchiol does bring a less-mobile presence to the field. But he does have experience. Marchiol started seven games during his four seasons at West Virginia, including the first four of 2025 before suffering a season-ending foot injury. He completed 66 of 98 passes (67.3%) for 720 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions last season while posting a 3-1 record for the Mountaineers. Iowa is coming off a 30-0 home shutout of then-No. 25 Wisconsin at Kinnick Stadium and needs to win its final four regular-season games to have a shot at the College Football Playoff. item.title: Player-coach rift report will only galvanise England - George
item.description: Jamie George (left) and captain Maro Itoje (right) are part of Steve Borthwick's senior leadership group [Getty Images] England hooker Jamie George says the squad are "really upset" by a newspaper article claiming the end of their summer tour was marked by player unrest over head coach Steve Borthwick's leadership. A report in the Times says unhappy players wanted summit talks with Borthwick and Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney in Argentina in July. It alleges there are disagreements among Borthwick's wider coaching group, which has been subject to frequent change in his nearly four years in charge, and concerns over the head coach's man-management skills. England meet Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, with George querying the timing of the article as well as its contents. The Saracens hooker, who was made England captain by Borthwick in 2024 before the role passed to Maro Itoje 12 months later, said that he did not recognise the situation described by the article. "I can tell you that a lot of it's untrue," George told Rugby Union Weekly. "We, as a squad, are incredibly disappointed by it. "You just have to look at the timing of the article - two days out from our first Test match. I think it's clearly there to try and be divisive. "It is the first time I think in my England career that as a group we've had to address an article that's been written, but we spoke about it brilliantly. "Maro called a leader's meeting and thought that that was the best way of us going about it. "Whoever's written this article, obviously their aim was for it to be divisive. Unfortunately for them, it's going to go the other way. "This is going to galvanise us, it's going to make us tighter. We speak a lot about standing up for people, we speak a lot about helping each other, and we've got to make sure that we do that for Steve. "He has had a bit of a personal attack here and an unwarranted one at that." item.title: Janja Garnbret conquered Bibliographie. Her next climb: unprecedented Olympic heights
item.description: Janja Garnbret made history on June 6 by becoming the first woman to climb Bibliographie, a 115-foot route on a limestone cliff in Céüse, France. Her sights are now set on another unprecedented feat — capturing two Olympic gold medals in climbing at one Games in Los Angeles in 2028. Garnbret, a 27-year-old from Slovenia, already won the combined at the Tokyo Games and the Paris Games, the first two Olympics to include her sport. "After both Olympics, I felt I like to call it a black period or something," she said. "I felt really unmotivated. I asked myself if I will ever be able to top again anything. Everybody prepares you for the competition, but no one really prepares you for what comes after. … I just needed to wait for the motivation to come back." Climbing had one competition in Tokyo — an event combining the disciplines of speed, boulder and lead. For Paris, it was split into two events — a combined event for boulder and lead plus an event for speed only. In LA, each of the three disciplines will have its own set of medals. "I think this is what we all wanted right from the beginning," Garnbret said. Garnbret began climbing whatever she could grasp by age 7 — trees, closets and doors. She has competed internationally in boulder and lead since age 14. She trained speed for the Tokyo Games, then dropped it from her repertoire afterward once it was no longer part of the Olympic combined event. In LA, the women's boulder and lead semifinals are back-to-back days, followed by a day off, and then back-to-back days of the finals. Garnbret has no preference between boulder and lead, having won the most recent world title in each in 2025. But this year, her focus was on Bibliographie. She recently toured the U.S. , promoting a film documenting her ascent. She said that only five people previously scaled it — all men. She trekked to it for the first time two weeks after the Paris Olympics. It took 21 sessions spread across the next two years to complete it. "I fell asleep thinking about the route," she said. "I woke up thinking about the route." Yet she still competed off and on in the Olympic disciplines on the World Series circuit in 2026. In five starts, she won three times and was runner-up the other two behind Zelia Avesou, a 22-year-old Frenchwoman, and Annie Sanders, a 19-year-old Texan. Women that young would have come through the ranks already knowing that climbing was an Olympic sport, unlike when Garnbret launched her career. "I do feel challenged," Garnbret said. "Competition is getting, of course, harder and harder." Garnbret hasn't decided yet whether she will continue on for the 2023 Brisbane Games, should climbing stay on the Olympic program. She does seek another challenge, though. Bibliographie is a 9b+ climb, the second-most difficult grade. item.title: LIV Golf Collapses As PGA Tour Sets Strict Return Rules
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images LIV Golf is officially finished. The league announced on Thursday that it will not restructure and is moving toward full liquidation after losing its financier, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund. This ends a period of division that split professional golf into competing tours. The answer depends on specific contractual obligations and the Tour’s stance on meritocracy. Brian Rolapp, the PGA Tour CEO, has made it clear that the path back is not automatic for anyone who defected. LIV officials announced they are ending the league this week, leaving players such as Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau with uncertain futures for the 2027 season. Rory McIlroy, the league’s most outspoken critic, took one last jab before the collapse. “They turned professional golf into an arms race,” McIlroy declared earlier this week, according to Yahoo Sports . The league’s demise leaves these stars without a tour, forcing them to consider other options. The DP World Tour remains a destination for some, as the current top 10 in the Race to Dubai secure PGA Tour cards. Patrick Reed adhered to this plan, restoring eligibility in August and improving his 2027 standing as a result. Others might pivot to YouTube golf, as DeChambeau has suggested he could focus on growing his channel three times over. The Return Rules Are Set The PGA Tour will not repeat the temporary solution used earlier this year. During a September press conference, Rolapp stated clearly, according to Yahoo Sports , “We are not currently contemplating a returning member program like the one you saw in January.” That specific program allowed Brooks Koepka to return ahead of the 2026 season. Koepka was reinstated through this one-time offer for golfers who “have been away from the (PGA) Tour for at least two years and have won The Players Championship, Masters Tournament, PGA Championship, U.S. Open or The Open Championship during the 2022-2025 seasons.” His penalties included not being eligible for any payment from the FedExCup bonus program for the 2026 season. Since that window has closed, other LIV players face a standard one-year suspension beginning at their last LIV tournament. According to reports, this precedent means players like Rahm would become eligible on Aug. 24, 2027, provided they have no other contractual ties. The CEO stressed that any player wishing to compete on the Tour required “to demonstrate that they are relieved of their contractual commitments or any tail obligations they might have in that legacy model.” Rolapp confirmed that Koepka had satisfied this requirement. item.title: Has the Detroit Lions defense turned a corner?
item.description: What a difference a month can make. After a historically bad start to the season, Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has helped the defense find their sea legs over the course of the last four weeks. With that said, there is still plenty to improve upon for a unit that has even more to play for with the loss of All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell during their Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings. There were some around the fan base and media who were ready to move on from Sheppard if things didn’t improve—especially after the loss to the Carolina Panthers where they appeared to be out-schemed from the jump. After some tough conversations as well as some schematic and personnel tweaks, the Lions’ defense is beginning to settle in dating back to their Week 5 whooping of the Arizona Cardinals. That brings us to today’s Question of the Day: Do you believe the Lions’ defense has turned a corner? My answer: Despite a three-game sample size not being the largest to go off of, I do belive this unit has begun to figure things out. It still isn’t perfect, and there are still too many missed assignments for my liking, but you can do a lot with the way the Lions’ front is playing. Their star players up front, like defensive end Aidan Hutchinson and defensive tackle Alim McNeill, are making their presence felt nearly every time the ball is snapped. Beyond those two, other members of the defensive line like rookie Skyler Gill-Howard and second year defensive tackle Tyleik Williams are playing some really good football. And while there are still things to clean up in the secondary, cornerback D.J. Reed’s play has really leveled out, star defensive back Brian Branch is back in the mix, and the team opened up All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph’s 21-day window last week. If they can continue to defend the run well and cut down on the blown coverage moments that have plagued them through seven games, I think that will be enough to make them a contender down the stretch. Continue to improve so that you are playing your best, and most sound football in December and into January. When you have an offense like Detroit does, that’s all you really need. What about you? item.title: John Gibson Returns to Practice With Detroit’s Net Unsettled
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have a goaltending decision to make before Saturday, and John Gibson practicing again just made it a harder one. Gibson was back on the ice Friday after leaving Tuesday’s game at Tampa Bay with a lower-body injury, Detroit Free Press reporter Helene St. James reported. He is still listed as day to day rather than cleared, so the question in front of Detroit is not only when Gibson is available, but whether he should get the net back when he is. Nov 3, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Detroit Red Wings goaltender John Gibson (36) makes a save during the first period against Tampa Bay Lightning at Benchmark International Arena. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) John Gibson Practiced, but He Is Not Cleared to Play St. James reported that Gibson took part in Friday’s practice, and nothing beyond that. Gibson missed Thursday’s game against the Vegas Golden Knights, and the reporting on his status stops short of Saturday , when the Red Wings open a road trip against the Colorado Avalanche on Nov. 7 . Detroit has not named a starter for that game. John Gibson Is Having a Bad Season for the Detroit Red Wings Gibson has played 11 games for the Red Wings this season. He has a 4-5-1 record with a 3.46 GAA and a .860 save percentage. Gibson has struggled big time and is 33 years old and in the final year of his contract , the eight-year deal he signed in Anaheim that carries a $6.4 million cap hit and sends him to unrestricted free agency this summer. He has not played well at all this season, and even though Gibson is back at practice, it may not be time for him to get the starting net back. Keep Daniil Tarasov and Michal Postava as the Goaltending Tandem Even if Gibson were to be healthy, the Red Wings should make him a healthy scratch. He provides nothing to the team at this point. A goaltending tandem of Daniil Tarasov and Michal Postava makes the Red Wings much more competitive between the pipes. Tarasov started for Detroit against the Vegas Golden Knights in a 2-1 loss on Thursday night , turning aside 32 shots in a game Detroit lost on a goal with 1:42 left . He has played in seven games this season for the Red Wings. Tarasov has a 2-2-2 record with a 1.79 GAA and a .930 save percentage, along with one shutout. He needs to be the starter for the rest of the season and Postava needs to get games as well. Gibson playing for the rest of the season will mean nothing for Detroit.

item.title: Utah State vs. Fresno State: How to watch, listen to or stream the game
item.description: Utah State quarterback McCae Hillstead (2) runs down the field as Colorado State cornerback CJ Blocker (17) defends Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in Logan. | Eli Lucero/Herald Journal Utah State (3-5, 2-2) vs. Fresno State (5-3, 3-1) Kickoff: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. MST Venue: Maverik Stadium TV: USA Sports Radio: Aggie Sports Network (KZNS 1280 The Zone) Series: Utah State and Fresno State have played 34 times since their first meeting in 1952. Fresno State leads all-time 19-14. Utah State has lost two of its last three games to the Bulldogs but won last year’s matchup, 28-17. The trends For Utah State: The Aggies are riding high after their performance against Colorado State last week. Utah State’s struggling offense has been the headliner all year, and it had a breakthrough with a season-high 31 points in a convincing 31-14 win. Quarterback McCae Hillstead made his first start since the season opener, and he looked great. Hillstead threw for 173 yards while completing 77% of his passes. He also ran for 79 yards on 11 carries and pulled in a 44-yard reception on a trick play from Anthony Garcia. Most importantly, Hillstead didn’t have any turnovers. The biggest caveat to all of this is that Colorado State is one of the worst defenses in the country. Still, it was the first time all year the offense was consistent on drives and moving the ball. For Fresno State: The Bulldogs are also coming off a confidence-boosting win over Oregon State, especially with how the previous few weeks went. Fresno State was rolling until it hosted Boise State in early October. The Bulldogs battled, but Boise State eked out a 38-31 win. Then the following week, Fresno State gave up 10 in the fourth quarter to San Diego State and lost 26-23. After a bye week, the Bulldogs were back in action and got a big 38-22 win over Oregon State. The Beavers were previously undefeated in Pac-12 play. What to watch for Is this a turning point for the offense? Utah State had its best offensive performance last week, and Hillstead looked the part of a starting quarterback. However, it’s difficult to determine if that result was because of natural offensive growth or because the Aggies played the statistically worst defense in the country. There’s probably truth somewhere in the middle, and Utah State will face a much tougher test against Fresno State. On average, the Bulldogs hold opponents to 21 points per game. That ranks 40th in the country. Meanwhile, Utah State averages just 17 points per game. Saturday will show if the offense has improved, if a healthy Hillstead is what it needed, or if the offense regresses to where it was before the Colorado State win. Protect the football and the quarterback: Utah State played some close games early in the season, and turnovers especially burned it against Idaho State and Washington. However, Hillstead and Grady Brosterhous have now gone three straight games without an interception. The last interception was one Hillstead threw against Boise State.

item.description: Quarterback Jacoby Brissett was traded from the Arizona Cardinals to the Baltimore Ravens, who have lost their two top quarterbacks to injuries (Stacy Revere) Baltimore completed a trade for 11-year NFL veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett on Friday, hours after the Ravens were routed by Jacksonville while using their third-string signal caller due to injuries. The Ravens made the deal for Brissett after losing star quarterback Lamar Jackson to a right thumb injury that will require surgery and backup Tyler Huntley for the season with a toe injury. Jackson's injury, which came on his first play back following an ankle injury, is "potentially" season-ending, Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. Rookie Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in Baltimore's 33-10 home loss Thursday to the Jaguars, which dropped the Ravens to 4-5 on the season. The club announced on social media the deal for Brissett, reportedly for a 2027 NFL Draft fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder while also obtaining a 2027 fifth-round selection and money. Brissett, 33, is expected to make his 74th career start and first for the Ravens when they return to the field on November 16 against the Los Angeles Chargers. "I feel like (Brissett) can come in and help us," Ravens running back Derrick Henry said. "We'll be excited to have him and we'll see where it goes." The Ravens have lost four games in a row with three different starting quarterbacks and been kept below 14 points in four consecutive games for the first time in club history. Brissett, a rookie backup to New England's Tom Brady in the Patriots' 2017 Super Bowl victory over Atlanta, will play for his seventh different NFL squad. item.title: Aaron Bates won’t be back as Dodgers hitting coach
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA - JULY 22, 2024: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Chris Taylor (3) works with Dodgers batting coach Aaron Bates before the game against the San Francisco Giants at Dodgers Stadium on July 22, 2024 in Los Angeles, CA.(Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) For the first time in three years, there will be a change in the Dodgers coaching staff for 2027, as hitting coach Aaron Bates won’t return. Tim Dierkes of MLB Trade Rumors was first to report the coaching change , which was also reported by Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times , Jack Harris of the California Post , and others. “The Dodgers offered Bates a multiyear contract to stay, but the two sides couldn’t agree to terms,” Dierkes wrote . Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman in his season-ending press conference at Dodger Stadium on October 21 was asked if there would be any coaching changes this offseason. “I expect status quo,” Friedman said. “We’re still working through some things, but expect status quo.” Bates, 42, was on the Dodgers major league coaching staff during the last eight seasons, including the last four as hitting coach along with Robert Van Scoyoc . Bates from 2019-22 held a dual role as assistant hitting coach on the major league staff and director of hitting for the minor league system . As a player, Bates was a third-round draft pick of the Boston Red Sox in 2006 out of North Carolina State, and he played in five games in the majors for Boston in 2009. The corner outfielder and first baseman played for nine seasons in the minors, ending with 11 games for Double-A Chattanooga in the Dodgers’ system in 2014. Bates was in the Dodgers organization for 13 years, including 12 years as a coach. Before joining the major league staff he was hitting coach in the Arizona Complex League in 2015 and 2016, then Class-A Great Lakes in 2017 , before shifting to assistant hitting coordinator for the Dodgers minors.
